item.title: Finals loom – School rugby’s finest battle for glory
item.description: After weeks of bruising schoolboy and schoolgirl rugby, the 2026 Vodafone Super Deans and Weet-Bix Raluve championships have produced their finalists, with eight national titles to be decided next week at the HFC Bank National Stadium in Suva. Suva Grammar School (SGS) is the best represented school, with three teams, under-16, U17 and U18, reaching the Super Deans finals.
item.content:encoded:
After weeks of bruising schoolboy and schoolgirl rugby, the 2026 Vodafone Super Deans and Weet-Bix Raluve championships have produced their finalists, with eight national titles to be decided next week at the HFC Bank National Stadium in Suva.

Suva Grammar School (SGS) is the best represented school, with three teams, under-16, U17 and U18, reaching the Super Deans finals.

Ratu Kadavulevu School (RKS), Queen Victoria School (QVS) and Lelean Memorial School (LMS) will each have two finalists.

Marist Brothers High School (MBHS) will be represented by its U15 side, while Ratu Navula College (RNC) is the lone Western school in the finals.

But the biggest story belongs to the North.

Navatu Secondary School carries the hopes of the entire Northern Division after becoming the first Northern school to reach a Super Deans final.

Navatu’s U19 side created history with a hard-fought 22-17 victory over RKS in the semi-final.

LMS earned its final place with a 36-27 win over RNC.

The other semi-finals produced their own drama.

QVS defeated Mahatma Gandhi Memorial High School (MGM) 22-15 in the U14, while Ratu Navula College edged Ratu Kadavulevu School 26-25.

In the U15, Ratu Kadavulevu School beat Queen Victoria School 28-26, while Marist Brothers High School accounted for Lelean Memorial School 16-3.

QVS defeated MGM 17-15 in the U16, while SGS shut out Nasinu Secondary School 22-0.

RKS defeated Ba Methodist High School 47-29 in the U17, with SGS beating QVS 32-24.

The Weet-Bix Raluve finals will feature Nasinu Secondary School against St Vincent College in the U16 and MGM against Lomary Secondary School in the U18.

For some schools, next week’s finals will be another chapter in a proud tradition.

For Navatu Secondary School, it is an opportunity to make history even greater.

– U16: Nasinu Secondary School v St Vincent College

item.title: Suva Grammar thumps Ra High
item.description: SUVA Grammar School produced a spectacular performance to storm into the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union U18 final after thumping Ra High School 51-0 at Churchill Park yesterday. Playing in front of an impressive crowd of around 8500 spectators, the Veiuto-based side dominated proceedings from the opening whistle, showcasing strong defence, attacking flair and composure across the park
item.content:encoded:
SUVA Grammar School produced a spectacular performance to storm into the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union U18 final after thumping Ra High School 51-0 at Churchill Park yesterday.

Playing in front of an impressive crowd of around 8500 spectators, the Veiuto-based side dominated proceedings from the opening whistle, showcasing strong defence, attacking flair and composure across the park.

Grammar took control in the opening 35 minutes and went into halftime with a commanding 24-0 lead.

Ra High struggled to find answers to Grammar’s intensity, with the Suva side continuing its relentless pressure after the break.

Grammar added another 27 points in the second half while completely shutting down Ra High in attack and defence.

Ra High was unable to build any meaningful momentum and was punished for lapses in defence and a lack of attacking execution as Grammar continued to pile on the pressure.

The win sets up a mouth-watering U18 final against Lelean Memorial School.

Grammar’s impressive campaign has been boosted by the experience of former Fiji Warriors and Suva representative Enele Malele, who is part of the coaching setup as the team’s strength and conditioning coach Sam Speight.

With the final now secured, Grammar will look to carry its dominant form into the title decider against Lelean.

item.title: Northern rugby’s historic dream nears reality
item.description: FOR years, Northern school rugby has carried the weight of being the forgotten force in Fiji’s high school competition. Now Navatu Secondary School has changed that narrative.
item.content:encoded:
FOR years, Northern school rugby has carried the weight of being the forgotten force in Fiji’s high school competition.

Now Navatu Secondary School has changed that narrative.

The Cakaudrove school created Vodafone Super Deans history by becoming the first Northern school to reach the under-19 final, earning a place among the country’s established schoolboy rugby powers.

From the qualifiers to the semi-final, Navatu had to overcome three of the biggest names in Fiji school rugby — Queen Victoria School, Suva Grammar School and Ratu Kadavulevu School.

Now only one stands between Navatu and a national title — Lelean Memorial School.

For head coach Alipate Ravulo, the journey has been the ultimate examination of a Northern school determined to make its name on the national stage.

“The journey to the final has been the ultimate test for us,” Ravulo said.

“We had to overcome three of the nation’s high school giants — QVS in the qualifiers, Suva Grammar in the quarter-final and a determined RKS in the semi-final.”

The achievement is made even more significant by what Navatu does not have.

The school has no rugby ground of its own.

For Ravulo, that remains the most heartbreaking part of the journey.

But it has also become a symbol of what Northern schools continue to overcome in their pursuit of recognition in Fiji schoolboy rugby.

“Our school does not have a school ground,” he said.

“For me, that is the most heartbreaking part, but it also shows the struggles and determination of Northern schools to make their name in high school rugby.”

Against RKS, Navatu entered as the underdog against a side accustomed to playing on the biggest stage.

“We came into the match as underdogs against a champion side like RKS, but we stuck to our game plan and held on for the win,” Ravulo said.

The 22-17 victory secured more than a place in the final.

But Ravulo knows history alone will not win the title.

Navatu must now prepare for Lelean Memorial School in the U19 final at the HFC Bank National Stadium in Suva.

The coach said his players would celebrate the achievement, but only briefly.

“We will enjoy it, but we will not take this opportunity lightly. We will go back to the drawing board, see what we need to polish from our semi-final victory and come back focused and ready to take on LMS.”

Navatu has already broken the Northern barrier.

Now it has the chance to break another — by finishing its historic campaign as national champions.

item.title: Rewa march on to semis
item.description: Rewa FC produced a memorable comeback at 4R Stadium,Govind Park in Ba yesterday, overcoming a 0-1 deficit to defeat Lae City FC 2-1 and secure a place in the OFC Men’s Champions League semi-finals. Needing nothing less than victory to keep their campaign alive, Rewa started with purpose and dominated possession and territory in the opening stages.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC produced a memorable comeback at 4R Stadium,Govind Park in Ba yesterday, overcoming a 0-1 deficit to defeat Lae City FC 2-1 and secure a place in the OFC Men’s Champions League semi-finals.

Needing nothing less than victory to keep their campaign alive, Rewa started with purpose and dominated possession and territory in the opening stages.

Despite their early pressure, the Delta Tigers were stunned when Lae City struck against the run of play through Raphael Rudolph after Solomon Kamake created the opening with a powerful run.

Rewa refused to panic and continued pushing forward in search of an equaliser.

Their persistence finally paid off in first-half stoppage time when captain Kavaia Rawaqa produced a moment of quality, turning onto his left foot before firing a superb long-range effort into the net to level the match 1-1 at halftime.

Rewa returned from the break with renewed confidence and completed the turnaround just seven minutes into the second half.

Merrill Nand became the hero, finding the bottom corner with a low effort after the ball broke kindly to him inside a crowded penalty area.

Lae City pushed for an equaliser, but Rewa defended resolutely while remaining dangerous on the counter.

The Delta Tigers held firm through late pressure, including a stoppage-time effort that struck the crossbar.

The victory sends Rewa into Wednesday’s semi-final at Govind Park, where they will face the winner of Group A.

item.title: South Africa edge Fijiana
item.description: SOUTH Africa Women XV held their nerve to secure a close 29-22 victory over the Vodafone Fijiana XV in the second Test at Churchill Park in Lautoka yesterday. The Fijiana XV made a strong start and took control of the first half, executing their game plan well to lead 10-5 at the break.
item.content:encoded:
SOUTH Africa Women XV held their nerve to secure a close 29-22 victory over the Vodafone Fijiana XV in the second Test at Churchill Park in Lautoka yesterday.

The Fijiana XV made a strong start and took control of the first half, executing their game plan well to lead 10-5 at the break.

Atelaite Buna and Adi Vani Buleki crossed the tryline for Fiji, while South Africa managed just one try through hooker Lindelwa Gwala.

However, South Africa returned from the break with tactical changes that helped turn the momentum in their favour.

Winger Maria Tshiremba proved the difference, scoring a hat-trick as the visitors fought their way back into the contest.

Tshiremba scored twice in the second half, with one conversion, as South Africa levelled the scores at 17-17 after 60 minutes.

Fijiana responded through Salote Nailolo, with Varanisese Qoro adding the conversion to keep the home side in the contest.

South Africa then regained the lead when Vainah Ubisi crossed for their fourth try, which was converted by fullback Byrhandre Dolf.

The Fijiana refused to give up and continued to attack, with Ivamere Nabura scoring their fourth try in the 74th minute.

Qoro was unable to convert, leaving the match still within reach for South Africa.

Tshiremba then completed her hat-trick in the 78th minute, scoring South Africa’s fifth try to seal the 29-22 victory.

South Africa captain Babalwa Latsha thanked the Fijian supporters for their strong backing of women’s rugby.

“Vinaka to all the Fijian fans supporting women’s rugby. We appreciate you all.”

Fijiana XV captain Kolora Lomani also thanked the supporters who turned up in numbers despite the result.

“We thank the man above. Even though we didn’t get the result, we thank our fans for coming out in numbers and also thank South Africa for coming to play with us.”

item.title: Kadavu makes historic Skipper Cup debut on home soil
item.description: YESTERDAY marked a historic chapter for Kadavu rugby as the Skipper Cup made its first appearance on the island, with Round Three matches played at Namalata Central School. The occasion gave the people of Kadavu the opportunity to witness Fiji’s premier provincial rugby competition on home soil, and the hosts made the most of the milestone by completing a clean sweep against Rewa.
item.content:encoded:
YESTERDAY marked a historic chapter for Kadavu rugby as the Skipper Cup made its first appearance on the island, with Round Three matches played at Namalata Central School.

The occasion gave the people of Kadavu the opportunity to witness Fiji’s premier provincial rugby competition on home soil, and the hosts made the most of the milestone by completing a clean sweep against Rewa.

The U20 side got the historic day underway with a determined 17-12 victory over Rewa.

It was followed by a dominant performance from the Kadavu Marama side, which produced the biggest win of the day with a commanding 48-0 result.

The senior grade then provided the day’s closest contest.

In a tense battle, Kadavu edged Rewa 18-17, holding on for a thrilling one-point victory to complete three wins from three matches.

While the results gave the home supporters plenty to celebrate, the significance of the day extended well beyond the scoreboard.

For the people of Kadavu, the arrival of the Skipper Cup represented an important milestone. Namalata Central School became the centre of provincial rugby, bringing together players, families, supporters and communities to witness a competition that is usually played outside the island.

For the first time, Kadavu’s rugby community did not have to travel elsewhere to experience the atmosphere of Skipper Cup rugby. The competition came to them.

And the home sides responded with performances that matched the occasion.

The U20 side showed resilience to secure its five-point victory, the Marama side delivered a dominant shutout, while the senior team kept its composure in a one-point thriller.

The three results also provided a fitting reward for the supporters who turned out to witness the historic occasion.

Round Three will therefore stand out in the Skipper Cup calendar for Kadavu, not only because of the results but because of what the day represented.

The tournament finally reached the island, Namalata Central School hosted a historic day of provincial rugby, and Kadavu responded by winning all three grades against Rewa.

For the people of Kadavu, yesterday was more than a day of rugby.

item.title: Kadavu Women rise to the occasion at home
item.description: Kadavu Women’s Rugby marked a historic home debut in the Subrails Marama Championship with a commanding 48–0 victory over Rewa at Namalata Central School yesterday. Playing in front of their home supporters, Kadavu produced a dominant performance to keep Rewa scoreless and turn their first appearance on home soil into a memorable occasion.
item.content:encoded:
Kadavu Women’s Rugby marked a historic home debut in the Subrails Marama Championship with a commanding 48–0 victory over Rewa at Namalata Central School yesterday.

Playing in front of their home supporters, Kadavu produced a dominant performance to keep Rewa scoreless and turn their first appearance on home soil into a memorable occasion.

Kadavu captain Ulumila Likubai said the team was grateful for the opportunity and thanked God for the result.

She said the victory was not necessarily what the team had intended or expected heading into the match, but she was thankful that the players were able to deliver the win on their home ground.

Likubai also thanked her teammates for their effort in bringing the victory home, making the occasion even more significant for the Kadavu players and the people who came out to support them.

The 48–0 scoreline reflected Kadavu’s control of the match, as Rewa struggled to find a response against a determined home side.

For Kadavu, the performance was not only about securing points. It was an opportunity to showcase women’s rugby in front of their own community during a historic round of the Skipper Cup.

The home side made full use of the occasion, while Rewa was left to reflect on a difficult match and the challenges that affected their preparation.

Rewa Marama manager Frances Qounadovu said she was proud of her players despite the heavy defeat, particularly after the team faced difficulties travelling to Kadavu.

“I’m proud of my girls today. They did exceptionally well,” Qounadovu said.

She revealed that Rewa only arrived in Kadavu on the morning of the match, reaching their venue at around 10am.

Qounadovu believes the long journey and limited recovery time affected the players before they took the field.

“We just arrived this morning and we reached our venue around about 10 this morning. I think that was a major contribution to the girls being jet-lagged,” she said.

However, she accepted that Rewa had areas to improve after being kept scoreless throughout the match.

“There was a lot of mistakes,” Qounadovu said, identifying technical execution and the team’s forwards as areas requiring greater attention.

“For me, I would say that it would be for us to go in better on some of our technical skills, especially with our forwards,” she said.

Qounadovu also acknowledged Kadavu’s performance, saying the home side put up a strong fight.

“I also would like to thank Kadavu Women’s Rugby. They did put out a big fight there,” she said.

The defeat leaves Rewa with plenty to work on before Round 4, but Qounadovu believes the campaign is not over.

“We know that in future we can still bring it back home. So there’s still hope there,” she said.

For Kadavu, however, the focus is on celebrating a special victory in front of their home crowd.

The 48–0 result gives the Kadavu women a memorable start to their historic home campaign and provides Likubai and her teammates with plenty of confidence heading into the next round.

While Rewa will return to training determined to correct the mistakes exposed by the match, Kadavu can take confidence from a clinical performance that saw them dominate the contest and finish with a clean sheet.

For the people of Kadavu, it was a day to remember — their women’s team delivering a convincing 48–0 victory on historic home soil.

item.title: Hosts Ba draw tough pool for BOG
item.description: THE Extra Supermarket Battle of the Giants pool stage is set for a fierce contest after four of the Extra Premier League’s top-ranked teams were drawn together in Pool B. The pools were drawn based on the standings after Round 14, which served as the qualifying round for the tournament.
item.content:encoded:
THE Extra Supermarket Battle of the Giants pool stage is set for a fierce contest after four of the Extra Premier League’s top-ranked teams were drawn together in Pool B.

The pools were drawn based on the standings after Round 14, which served as the qualifying round for the tournament.

In pool A are Labasa, Nasinu, Suva, Navua and in pool B are Ba, Rewa, Lautoka and Nadi.

Fiji Football Association chief executive Mohammed Yusuf described Pool B as the “pool of death”, with two teams set to exit the competition after the pool stage.

“Two top teams will exit the competition after pool games,” Yusuf said.

Pool B features teams ranked first, second, fourth and seventh in the Extra Premier League, setting up a demanding battle for the two semi-final places.

Yusuf said the strength of the pool means every match will carry the intensity of a final.

“The pool games in Pool B is like a final every day. On Friday, Saturday and Sunday afternoon, you will see a top-class battle between the top teams,” he said.

With only two teams able to progress from each pool, the margin for error will be small for the sides considered among the leading contenders.

Yusuf believes the draw could produce a high-quality tournament, with the strongest teams expected to face each other before the semi-finals.

Meanwhile, the other pool is expected to provide a more evenly matched contest, giving teams there an opportunity to battle for the remaining semi-final places.

The Battle of the Giants will therefore provide an early test for the leading Extra Premier League sides, with Pool B likely to determine which contenders can handle the pressure and progress to the final stages.

The 2026 BOG will take place at the 4R Govind Park Stadium in Ba, September 4-6 for the knockout stages and September 12-13 for the finals.

Recent dominance: Labasa(Won 4 out of last 6 titles.)
